01.r: The officers belonged to Solomon's administration.
01.n: Literally 'and to Solomon', the Hebrew way of saying 'Solomon had'. Gesenius: Solomon, David's son and successor, the third king of the Israelites, very celebrated for his riches, splendour and wisdom.

02.n: Hebrew writes twelve as 'two ten'; both words are counted here in 'twelve'.

03.n: Gesenius: this form is only used in numbers compounded with ten, eleven to nineteen.

04.r: Royal officials set over the districts of the land.
04.n: A participle, literally 'ones stationed'. Gesenius: an officer, director, citing this verse; BDB: deputy, prefect, as appointed. The DRC and BSB say 'governors'.

05.r: Their authority covered the whole land.

06.r: No part of Israel was left out.

08.r: The officers kept the court supplied with food.
08.n: The brief's lexicon gives 'to sustain, support, nourish' for this form; Gesenius gives the root sense as to measure, and for this form to hold, to contain, to sustain. YLT says 'sustained'; the KJV 'provided victuals'.

09.r: Marks 'the king' as the one provided for.
09.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'the king'.

11.r: Adds the household, with the object marker again.
11.n: 'And' with the object marker; counted here with 'his household'.

12.r: Everyone who lived and ate at the king's court.
12.n: Literally 'his house'; BDB includes the sense house as containing a family, including household affairs, persons and property.

13.r: One month's supply for each officer.
13.n: Gesenius: the new moon, and so the lunar month that began with it.

15.r: The duty came round to each in turn, year by year.
15.n: An imperfect, here for something that happened regularly: 'it would be'. YLT: 'is'.

16.r: The duty rested on each officer.
16.n: Literally 'upon': the month was a charge laid on each one.

17.n: Literally 'the one', used distributively: each one.

18.r: To supply the court for his month.
18.n: The same verb as 'they provided for' earlier in the verse, here as an infinitive.

02.n: δώδεκα, twelve: one Greek word for the two Hebrew words.

08.n: χορηγέω, to supply, furnish; the Greek makes it an infinitive, 'to supply'.
